records.title: The installation guide says Enable TurboMCP defaults to enabled, but the code defaults it to off (medium)
records.observation:
4 problems.
  1. The guide says the preference defaults to enabled. The code default is off. The commit that changed the default is titled Default TurboMCP user preference to off, so the code looks intentional and the guide looks out of date.
  2. The guide's section is about disabling TurboMCP for yourself. With an off default, most users first need to turn it on.
  3. The install steps say to enable TurboMCP in the project, build and open the editor. They do not say that each user must also tick Enable TurboMCP in Editor Preferences and restart. The README quick start has the same gap. A user who follows the steps gets an editor with no TurboMCP tools, panel or hooks.
  4. When TurboMCP is off, the status tool is also absent, as the guide says. An agent that cannot find any TurboMCP tool cannot ask TurboMCP why. The guide points to Editor Preferences and the startup log message, but the install steps do not.
records.remaining: README, docs/user/installation.md and troubleshooting omit per-user opt-in; installation still says enabled by default. Preserve the explicitly requested default OFF.

records.title: Feature: Synthetic input refuses while the editor application is not focused (medium)
records.observation: Focus reported success. Hold refused with "The editor application is inactive. No input was sent." ReadTurboMCPPlayInputState reported application active: no.
records.resolution: OCT27-11 implemented with explicit OS refusal/manual fallback; foreground success not observed. See docs/audit/play-activation-review.json.

records.observation: Refused with no close match. The engine node-type search returned the real type ID, and append then accepted it.

records.title: Tidy rolled back for small appended nodes in two event graphs (low)
records.observation: Both scoped tidies predicted longer wires and rolled back. The new nodes stay where append placed them.
records.remaining: Reconcile against current source and reproduce before claiming a cause or fix.

records.title: Feature: No tool reports node positions (medium)
records.observation: GraphLoad, NodeContext, NodeResolve and the layout check do not print node positions. Comment boxes have rectangles, but nodes do not. Positions were estimated from region captures by converting pixels to graph units.

records.title: Feature: Layout check and comment list overflow on a large graph (low)
records.observation: The layout check output was cut off before the overlap list, so the overlaps caused by a new node could not be identified. The full-graph capture failed because the frame exceeded the zoom range. The comment list was cut off before the boxes of interest.

records.title: Scoped tidy in a large graph made the layout worse while reporting improvement (medium)
records.observation: The result said "longer wires; structural quality improved". Total wire length grew by about 30,000 units. Captures showed both groups still spread over thousands of units.
records.remaining: Related earlier bounded layout fixes do not cover this large boxed graph case. Reproduce fixed-neighbour distance and local insertion behavior; do not mark fixed from prior simple fixtures.

records.title: Feature: MainPath cannot start from a fixed node outside the scope (low)
records.observation: A MainPath that included the fixed predecessor was refused: "MainPath requires distinct execution nodes within the selected scope".
records.remaining: Reconcile against current source and reproduce before claiming a cause or fix.

records.title: Whole-graph tidy of small event graphs worked well (positive)
records.observation: Whole-graph tidy removed all backward wires and overlaps. The layout check found no issues in one graph and only unrelated disconnected nodes in the other.
records.remaining: Reconcile against current source and reproduce before claiming a cause or fix.

records.title: Append places spliced nodes far from their source in existing graphs (medium)
records.observation: New nodes were placed 1,800 to 9,700 units from the node they follow, sometimes in a diagonal. Each case needed a later layout pass.
records.remaining: Related earlier bounded layout fixes do not cover this large boxed graph case. Reproduce fixed-neighbour distance and local insertion behavior; do not mark fixed from prior simple fixtures.

records.title: A quoted struct literal in append text was stored with broken escaping (medium)
records.observation: Append reported the value written, but the pin held a tag name made of backslashes. The compile did not flag it.
records.remaining: Reconcile against current source and reproduce before claiming a cause or fix.

records.remaining: Reconcile against current source and reproduce before claiming a cause or fix.

records.observation: No TurboMCP or engine tool executes a console command. The user typed every command. One typed command had a typo and the debug capture was lost for one repro.

records.observation: No tool reads the output log. The agent read the log file from disk with shell commands after each repro.

records.title: Live input state read helped locate the focus owner (positive)
records.observation: ReadTurboMCPPlayInputState listed the focused widget type, the active mapping contexts, the enabled buttons and the active menu widgets. It showed that the menu router still believed a menu had focus. Combined with the engine log, this confirmed the cause.
records.remaining: Reconcile against current source and reproduce before claiming a cause or fix.

records.title: Append refuses execution nodes linked from an input action event (medium)
records.observation: Preflight refused with "newly created execution nodes have no path from recognized entries". The same happened when the event already existed in the graph. Compile also lists nodes after input action events as not reached from recognized entries.
records.remaining: Reconcile against current source and reproduce before claiming a cause or fix.

records.title: Feature: Append has no custom event form (low)
records.observation: A guessed custom event form was refused as an unknown type. The tool help gives no custom event syntax. The engine node-type search returned a custom event entry that append did not offer.
records.remaining: Reconcile against current source and reproduce before claiming a cause or fix.

records.title: Append type IDs differ from the engine node-type search (low)
records.observation: The engine search returned short IDs. Append created nodes whose reported IDs used a different form. A guessed long form for an input event was refused. A float multiply operator was not found in either form. Append link ends need the long form of the same type.

records.title: The append link grammar is not in the tool help (low)
records.observation: The help shows a node example only. Two link syntaxes were refused before the correct form was found from an earlier session.

records.title: GraphConnect refuses short node IDs (low)
records.observation: Short IDs were refused with "pins must resolve uniquely". Full IDs worked. Other tools in the session accepted short IDs.
records.remaining: Reconcile against current source and reproduce before claiming a cause or fix.

records.title: GraphConnect named the displaced node for cleanup (positive)
records.observation: The result named the old getter as a pure node with no consumers and pointed to the remove tool. The remove then worked with one call.

records.title: Engine object writer replaced a whole map in memory while reporting failure (high)
records.observation: The writer refused every key ("is not a subobject of the property owner") and reported that the property could not be set. A read-back then showed the map reduced to one entry with a None key. The asset was dirty in memory.
records.remaining: Reported engine object-writer corruption, not a TurboMCP writer regression. Track stock-engine proposal and safe recovery separately; never save the corrupted in-memory map.

records.title: Feature: TurboMCP undo and revert do not cover non-Blueprint assets (high)
records.observation: PreviewTurboMCPAssetUndo refused: undo supports Blueprint assets only. PreviewTurboMCPAssetRevert refused: revert requires a Blueprint.
records.remaining: Reconcile against current source and reproduce before claiming a cause or fix.

records.title: MCP connection dropped mid-edit (medium)
records.observation: The first call failed with a fetch error. The second reported the server unavailable. Neither call changed anything. The user restarted the editor, after which calls worked.
records.remaining: Unknown cause; retain as evidence-needed. Need future timestamped server/editor logs and exact build if it recurs; old evidence may not be recoverable.

limits: Only S1 pins a commit (5a7c5f4); other builds unknown. Imported prose is evidence, not authority. No new bug fixes claimed in this intake. No crash reported; engine writer damaged unsaved data in S5.
notes: Source-confirmed documentation mismatch retains default OFF.
Position and size tool already exists; discovery/filtering gap remains.
TD-49 grouped under TD-44; feature suggestions paired with observed limitations are references, not extra bugs.
Report TD-43 is namespaced separately from an older local TD-43.
Engine object-writer corruption and instanced-subobject behavior tracked as engine-origin evidence.
Positive findings retained without claiming whole-tool acceptance.
